title: TokenSeek: Memory Efficient Fine Tuning via Instance-Aware Token Ditching
claim: Activations dominate training memory, and our method reaches better performance at a fraction of the memory of competing approaches.
layout: 2 panels, left donut charts to right scatter plot, nested rings
description: Two panels. Panel (a) shows two nested donut charts of Llama3 8B training memory at batch size 1 and batch size 8. The inner ring splits memory into parameters (green), gradients and optimizer states (blue), and activations (red). The outer ring breaks it down further into loss, gradients and optimizer. Activations grow from 50% to 87% as batch size increases. Panel (b) is a scatter plot of performance against memory, from 10% to 100%. Distinct markers show TokenSeek (green, bold in the legend), TokenTune, LoHa, QLoRA and the baseline. Dashed green arrows point from the baseline to TokenSeek variants. The TokenSeek markers sit at the top left, with high performance and low memory. The legend on the right explains the markers.
caption: Motivation behind TOKENSEEK and its preliminary comparison. (a) Breakdown of training memory under different batch side settings, revealing that activations are the primary bottleneck in training memory consumption. (b) Effective and efficient TOKENSEEK (ours) vs. concurrent arts in performance and memory consumption on Llama3.2 1B (detailed results in Tab. 1)
abstract: Fine tuning has been regarded as a de facto approach for adapting large language models (LLMs) to downstream tasks, but the high training memory consumption inherited from LLMs makes this process inefficient. Among existing memory efficient approaches, activation-related optimization has proven particularly effective, as activations consistently dominate overall memory consumption. Although prior arts offer various activation optimization strategies, their data-agnostic nature ultimately results in ineffective and unstable fine tuning. In this paper, we propose TokenSeek, a universal plugin solution for various transformer-based models through instance-aware token seeking and ditching, achieving significant fine-tuning memory savings (e.g., requiring only 14.8% of the memory on Llama3.2 1B) with on-par or even better performance. Furthermore, our interpretable token seeking process reveals the underlying reasons for its effectiveness, offering valuable insights for future research on token efficiency.
